title: Evaluation of the Patient App as a Complementary e-Health Intervention in Mobile Geriatric Rehabilitation (MoGeRe): A Mixed-Methods Study
summary:
Background: The number of older people in Germany is growing. The number of very old people, in particular, is rising. Experts say that by 2040, about one in four people will be over the age of 70. At the same time, the total population of Germany is declining. This creates challenges in funding healthcare and long-term care.
Older people often take longer to recover from an illness. They also face a higher risk of needing long-term care. That is why it is very important for them to remain independent for as long as possible. Rehabilitation measures can help with this.
In Bavaria, geriatric rehabilitation usually takes place in a hospital or a rehabilitation facility. However, there is another option: mobile geriatric rehabilitation (MoGeRe). In this case, patients are treated at home.
This form of treatment has advantages:
•    People remain in their familiar surroundings.
•    The treatment costs less money.
•    Quality of life can be better.
•    The work is often more pleasant for professionals as well.
Mobile services are flexible and incur fewer fixed costs. They can help solve problems such as a shortage of skilled workers and rising care needs.
Despite the advantages, there are also challenges:
1. Time between treatments
Treatment takes place on average three days a week. That amounts to about 200 minutes of therapy per week. There are breaks between appointments. These breaks are important so that patients do not overexert themselves.
However: Patients must practice on their own during this time. To do so, they need motivation and support. Digital solutions, such as telemedicine, can help with this. They enable contact with the treatment team.
2. Distance between home and the facility
Patients are at home and not under constant observation. If their condition worsens, a quick response is needed. Telemedicine can help, for example through video calls. This allows questions to be clarified quickly. Family members can also be better involved.
3. Scheduling appointments
Many patients find it difficult to organize their appointments.
Digital apps can help:
•    They display all appointments.
•    They notify users of changes.
•    They show exactly when staff will arrive.
This helps avoid waiting times and makes it easier to plan daily life.
The planned app helps with key organizational and communication challenges. It uses modern technology, prioritizes data protection, and is easy to use.
This makes care for older adults at home better, simpler, and tailored to the patients.

Methodology: The study is expected to run for all participants throughout the entire duration of the mobile rehabilitation program.
The team will assess whether patients are suitable for the study. After signing the consent form, participants will receive a code word for all surveys. They will also receive access to an initial survey. This is a short questionnaire in paper&pencil form.
Participants in the groups using the app will now receive the app on their (loaned) device. Then the mobile rehabilitation program begins.
After 3 weeks, there is another short written survey. The code word is required for this.
After completion of the rehabilitation, there is a final short written survey, for which the code word is required again.
In addition, after completion of the rehabilitation, individuals from each group will be randomly selected and invited for a personal interview.
conditions: primarily geriatric patients, possibly with multimorbidity typical of geriatric patients, with a valid prescription for mobile geriatric rehabilitation

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients:
- Valid prescription and certificate of coverage for a mobile geriatric rehabilitation program
- Mild cognitive impairment / mild delirium
- No hearing loss or mild to moderate hearing loss
- No visual impairment or mild to moderate visual impairment
- Living situation: living at home
- Sufficient written and spoken German language skills

Employees:
- Employee of MoRe-Life GmbH
- No mental health conditions
- No cognitive impairments
- Sufficient written and spoken German language skills
Exclusion criteria:
Patients:
- No current prescription and no certificate of coverage for a Mobile Geriatric Rehabilitation Program (MoGeRe)
- Severe mental illnesses and/or impairments such as:
         - Psychosis
         - Schizophrenia
         - Severe depression
         - Severe anxiety disorder
         - Dementia
- Moderate to severe cognitive impairments
- Severe hearing loss bordering on deafness, deafness, provided that no relatives are available to assist with using the app
- Severe visual impairment, blindness, provided that no relatives are available to assist with using the app
- Living situation: living in a nursing home, in short-term care at a nursing home
- Insufficient written and spoken German language skills

Employees:
- No employees of MoRe-Life GmbH
- Serious mental illnesses and/or impairments such as:
         - Psychosis
         - Schizophrenia
         - Severe depression
         - Severe anxiety disorder
         - Dementia
- Insufficient written and spoken German language skills
